page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-4 is an entry-tier compute-oriented instance provisioned on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, supported by 2 threads per core. Memory allocation is set at 4.0 GB of RAM, equating to 1.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache specifications include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Vector processing supports standard AVX instructions, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are omitted.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng recording a score of 2688.77, placing it in the top quartile of tested instances. However, parallel throughput is constrained by the limited core count, resulting in lower-tier placement on multithreaded evaluations including Geekbench multi-core (3311.0) and PassMark CPU (6160.65). Memory performance exhibits a similar divide; while uncached large-block reads (43.63 GB/sec) and writes (30.48 GB/sec) deliver middle-tier throughput, overall memory benchmarks such as the PassMark memory score (1081.99) and cached read bandwidth rank in the lower brackets.

The 1.0 GB per core ratio establishes high compute density relative to memory footprint, offering operational cost efficiency for tasks requiring focused CPU cycles without memory-heavy overheads. The architectural tradeoff centers on capacity: applications with elevated memory footprints or heavy parallel thread pools will face strict hardware limits. Consequently, the n2d-highcpu-4 is best matched with lightweight batch processing, single-threaded computational tasks, microservices, and modest CI/CD pipeline workers.
